 IndiGo expects first Airbus A350 delivery in second quarter of 2028, CEO Willie Walsh says
 SECTIONS IndiGo expects first Airbus A350 delivery in second quarter of 2028, CEO Willie Walsh says ET Online Last Updated: Nov 02, 2026, 11:27:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis The anticipated delivery of IndiGo's first Airbus A350 wide-body aircraft is scheduled for the second quarter of 2028, according to CEO Willie Walsh. The airline is focused on expanding its long-haul routes despite the hurdles of increasing fuel costs and a falling rupee. To better manage its operations, IndiGo has cut back on its Saudi Arabia routes.

 IndiGo to receive first Airbus A350 aircraft in 2028 as airline plans long-haul expansion: CEO Willie Walsh
 IndiGo expects to receive its first Airbus A350 wide-body aircraft in the second quarter of calendar year 2028, CEO Willie Walsh said on Monday, as the airline seeks to expand its long-haul international operations.
 As per Reuters, speaking at his first in-person briefing since taking charge as chief executive in August, Walsh said IndiGo had “incredible opportunities” despite a challenging operating environment for the airline industry.
 Also Read: Government notifies new airfare rules, allows intervention in extraordinary situations 
“We see incredible opportunities,” he said.
Walsh said IndiGo had the necessary foundations to succeed in the long-haul market. The airline’s plans for the A350 are part of its broader international expansion strategy. He also said the carrier would continue discussions with Boeing in case future opportunities arise.
 Live Events
 The airline industry is facing pressure from rising fuel prices, while the depreciation of the rupee has added to costs for Indian carriers. IndiGo reported a net loss of Rs 1,879.1 crore in the September quarter, with higher fuel expenses and the weaker rupee affecting profitability. The airline also reduced capacity during the period.
 “Airline industry situation challenging; we will continue to navigate through challenges,” Walsh said. "Airport charges are too high; Indian market will do much better with lower charges, taxes."
 Also Read: IndiGo posts Rs 1,879-crore loss as high fuel costs, geopolitical woes hit; capacity cuts & yield management offer only partial relief, says CEO Willie Walsh 
IndiGo has reduced its flights to Saudi Arabia by around 30 flights a day, according to Reuters.
On the Navi Mumbai airport, Walsh said the facility represented a significant opportunity for IndiGo. He added that the airline’s decision to shift some international flights there was taken in the company’s interest.
IndiGo currently operates more than 2,100 flights a day and has an operational fleet of over 400 aircraft. The airline’s use of Boeing 787 aircraft for international expansion offers an indication of how it could deploy the A350s, Walsh said.
